messages.content: Write a post about why a company is investing in developer relations. Around 250 words.

# Why we're hiring for developer relations

We're building a developer relations team. Here's the reasoning.

Look at where our new customers came from this past year: most read the docs, tried the SDK, or watched a conference talk before anyone from sales talked to them. That's the default path now, not the exception. If a developer can't figure out our API from the documentation alone, we lose them before a salesperson gets a chance.

Support tickets back this up. A large share of what comes in isn't about bugs — it's missing examples, confusing error messages, and gaps between what the docs say and what the SDK does. Nobody's owned those problems full time until now.

The plan: rewrite the docs, replace stub snippets with real example code, and put engineers in Discord and GitHub issues answering questions as they come in. We also want people who sit in on customer calls and carry what they hear back to the product team — some of our best fixes started as an offhand comment from a developer stuck debugging at 11pm.

This isn't a marketing hire. The team reports through engineering. Success means fewer support tickets, less time between signup and a working first request, and docs developers trust enough to stop asking us things we already answered.

If you've done this work before, we want to talk to you.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
